S7 class for fixed cognitive parameter specifications

Source: R/S7-fixed.R
MVBU_FixedParameter.Rd

Represents fixed parameter specifications in a dual-space (original vs. transformed cue space) framework, supporting declarative parameter fixing across global, category-specific, and cue-specific cognitive parameters.

Constructs a fixed parameter specification for fit_ideal_adaptor. Supports fixing parameters globally, per-category, or per-cue, in either original or transformed cue space.

Usage

MVBU_FixedParameter(
  par_class = character(),
  value = list(),
  category = character(),
  cue = character(),
  cue_space = character()
)

fix_parameter(
  value,
  class = c("m_0", "S_0", "kappa_0", "nu_0", "expected_mu_0", "expected_Sigma_0", "mu_0",
    "Sigma_0", "lapse_rate", "lapse_bias", "category_prior", "weights"),
  category = NULL,
  cue = NULL,
  cue_space = c("original", "transformed")
)

# S3 method for class 'MVBU_FixedParameter'
x[i, ...]

Arguments

par_class

Character vector of parameter classes (e.g., "m_0", "S_0", "kappa_0", "nu_0", "expected_mu_0", "expected_Sigma_0", "mu_0", "Sigma_0", "lapse_rate", "lapse_bias", "category_prior", "weights").

value

Numeric value, vector, matrix, or character assignment (e.g., "lapse_rate = 0.05").

category

Character string specifying category name (default: "" or NULL for all categories).

cue

Character string specifying cue name (default: "" or NULL for all cues).

cue_space

Character string specifying cue space: "original" (default) or "transformed".

class

Character string specifying parameter class: "m_0", "S_0", "kappa_0", "nu_0", "expected_mu_0", "expected_Sigma_0", "mu_0", "Sigma_0", "lapse_rate", "lapse_bias", "category_prior", or "weights".

x

An MVBU_FixedParameter object.

i

Indices specifying elements to extract.

...

Additional arguments (ignored).

Value

An object of class MVBU_FixedParameter.

A subsetted MVBU_FixedParameter object.

Category Moment Parameter Interpretations

When fixing category representation parameters, note the distinction between prior hyperparameters, expected prior moments, and known category parameters:

"m_0" and "S_0"

Prior hyperparameters of the conjugate prior distribution (Normal-Inverse-Wishart or Normal-Inverse-Chi-squared). "m_0" is the prior category mean vector (center of the normal prior on \(\mu_0\)), and "S_0" is the prior scatter matrix.

"expected_mu_0" and "expected_Sigma_0"

Expected moments of category representations under the prior. For category means, \(E[\mu_0] = m_0\), so "expected_mu_0" is canonicalized directly to "m_0". For covariance matrices, \(E[\Sigma_0] = S_0 / (\nu_0 - K - 1)\) for NIW (or \(E[\Sigma_0] = S_0 / (\nu_0 - 2)\) for NIX/MNIX). Specifying "expected_Sigma_0" allows users to fix the intuitive expected covariance. Stan input preparation automatically rescales this value to the conjugate scatter matrix "S_0" given \(\nu_0\).

"mu_0" and "Sigma_0"

Truly known category representation parameters entering the model as fixed, non-random constants without latent prior parameters. Fixing either or both moments determines the conjugate belief updating and the predictive likelihood behavior:

Case 1 (both unknown)

Standard NIW or NIX conjugate updating for both mean and covariance; the predictive likelihood is Student-\(t\).

Case 2 ("Sigma_0" known, "mu_0" unknown)

Category covariance is fixed to \(\Sigma_0\). Category mean is updated via Normal-mean updating (\(\kappa_n = \kappa_0 + n\), \(\mu_n = (\kappa_0 m_0 + n \bar{x}) / \kappa_n\)). Because the covariance is known without uncertainty, the predictive likelihood is Normal with covariance \((1 + 1/\kappa_n) \Sigma_0\).

Case 3 ("mu_0" known, "Sigma_0" unknown)

Category mean is fixed to \(\mu_0\). Category covariance is updated via Inverse-Wishart (NIW) or Inverse-Chi-squared (NIX) around the known mean (\(\nu_n = \nu_0 + n\), \(S_n = S_0 + \sum (x_i - \mu_0)(x_i - \mu_0)^T\)). Because the mean is known, the predictive likelihood is Student-\(t\) with \(\nu_n\) degrees of freedom and scale \(S_n / (\nu_n - K + 1)\) (or \(S_n / \nu_n\) for NIX).

Case 4 (both "mu_0" and "Sigma_0" known)

Both category moments are known and fixed. No belief updating occurs with exposure, and the predictive likelihood is Normal with mean \(\mu_0\) and covariance \(\Sigma_0\).

See also

parameter_prior, fit_ideal_adaptor

Examples

# Fix cognitive parameters
fix_kappa <- fix_parameter(value = 10, class = "kappa_0")
fix_nu <- fix_parameter(value = 5, class = "nu_0")
fix_lapse <- fix_parameter(value = 0.02, class = "lapse_rate")

# Combine fixed parameters
c(fix_kappa, fix_nu, fix_lapse)
#> MVBU_FixedParameter with 3 specification(s):
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   class      category cue   cue_space value
#>   <chr>      <chr>    <chr> <chr>     <chr>
#> 1 kappa_0    (all)    (all) original  10   
#> 2 nu_0       (all)    (all) original  5    
#> 3 lapse_rate (all)    (all) original  0.02
